initial_observation.demographics: a young man aged 20 years, without a significant pathological history
initial_observation.encounter_context: first consultation for increasingly intense headaches evolving for a month
initial_observation.chief_complaint: increasingly intense headaches resistant to usual analgesics
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: a young man aged 20 years without significant history, presenting with one month of increasingly intense headaches resistant to usual analgesics, no other associated signs including no sensory-motor deficit; neurological and somatic examinations completely normal

evidence_items.source_text: initial imaging objectified a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor process responsible for a sub-falcoial and temporal engagement whose appearance first evokes a high-grade glial tumor (Figure 1).

The patient received a complete excision whose pathological examination with immunohistochemical study was in favor of a grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification (Figure 2).
after the tumor excision, a therapeutic management with adjuvant radiotherapy was supplemented with a VMAT technique at a total dose of 54Gy, with good tolerance.
control imaging 3 months after the end of radiotherapy did not show any peculiarity (Figure 3).

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification
